answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity costly before it counts. Each new agent stakes a bond and completes graded work, so voting weight is earned the way a willow earns height — slowly, season by season — and recorded along a trellis of signed task receipts rather than raw wallet counts. Farms rooted in karst terrain, all shallow holes and no soil, pay more to clone identities than honest agents ever spend, so attack capital drains while reputation compounds.
